messages:
karen: FYI new onboarding step uses the docker-based localtest image (redwood/localtest:latest) but the new hire couldn't get their profile to be picked up. They mounted `~/.config/redwood:/home/dev/.config/redwood` and started the container, passed `--profile=dev-scratch` and it still used the image-provided profile 'container-default'.

devon: do we ship a profile inside the docker image under /etc/redwood/profile?

sam: yes the image has /etc/redwood/profile to simplify quickstarts. But mounting the host dir should take precedence. Can you share `ls -la` inside the container on the mounted path?

karen: inside container `ls -la /home/dev/.config/redwood` shows files owned by uid 1001 (host user) and container process is running as uid 1000. So the CLI can't read the config files due to permission denied, and the resolver falls back to /etc/redwood/profile.

karen: quick trace: 
```
[resolver] scanning /etc/redwood/profile -> found name: container-default
[resolver] scanning /home/dev/.config/redwood/profile -> open error: permission denied
[resolver] requested_profile: dev-scratch
[resolver] selected: container-default (fallback)
```

devon: ah that explains it. The Docker image runs as non-root uid 1000 and typical host mounts can be uid-mismatched. We should detect unreadable user configs and log a clear warning rather than silently falling back.

sam: Agreed. Two changes: 1) make resolver emit WARN when candidate config exists but is unreadable and mention path + permission bits in debug logs; 2) in localtest docs call out `--user $(id -u):$(id -g)` when running the image or use `chown -R` on the mounted dir.

infra-packaging: Packaging note: we ship an example profile in the image for quickstart but we can avoid active client ids there. Filed PKG-339 to update container image to include examples under `/usr/share/redwood/examples` and keep `/etc/redwood` empty or minimal.

karen: new-hire workaround: `docker run --user $(id -u):$(id -g) -v ~/.config/redwood:/home/dev/.config/redwood redwood/localtest:latest redwoodctl localtest start --profile=dev-scratch` — that made the CLI read the host profile.

sam: I'll add a resolver change: try to open each candidate and if open fails due to EACCES/EISDIR log a warning and continue scanning for other matches (but do not silently prefer /etc). Also add a user-facing error when requested_profile provided but not found in any readable location.

ci-bot: PR #1402 created adding permission-aware resolver logs + quickstart doc update. CI queued.

infra-packaging: I'll coordinate an image update to avoid shipping a usable profile and add a note in the localtest README about Docker UID mismatches.

karen: thanks everyone. New hire unblocked once we ran container as their uid. Leaving note in onboarding checklist. :thumbsup:
